newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended a bit lower but well above previous lows as an upward shift in European debt markets lifted bonos higher in the afternoon.
"At the end, France's announcements had little impact," one trader in Madrid said.
France said its 1997 buget deficit was running at 3.5 to 3.7 percent of gross domestic product, adding that it was preparing measures to cut it by 0.4 percent.
Although the Spanish market bounced back, other dealers in Madrid stressed that trading volume was really low, and said that the underlying mood was turning negative.
"Short run the market could gain, but to me it's more than clear it's time to sell, at least in the medium term," said Jose Ramon Arechederra, trader at ABN Amro in Madrid.
He said the long-bond future was sending a sell signal having failed repeatedly to go above 118.
The Spanish 10-year spread over Bunds fell to 64 basis points, little changed from Friday's ending level of 65, but down from 67 points it reached on France's announcements.
"I guess the spread is going to stay where it is unless they announce a delay in EMU's start," Arechederra said.
